newsitem.title: USA: Fla. courts Calif. film-industry decision-makers.
newsitem.headline: Fla. courts Calif. film-industry decision-makers.

text.p: Gov. Lawton Chiles will host a Beverly Hills, Calif. party next month to court Hollywood film-industry decision-makers with strong Florida ties, an aide said on Tuesday.
"We want to say, 'We're working real hard to get you to come home'," said John Reitzammer, executive director of the Florida Entertainment Industry Council.
Chiles several years ago created the council, a public and private venture, to boost film production in Florida and has set a target of $1 billion in Hollywood spending by 2000.

Teams working on feature films, commercials and television shows spent an estimated $600 million in Florida last year, up from $597 million in 1995, the council said. Florida ranks after California and New York as a U.S. entertainment center.

The council scoured electronic databases and other sources for actors, directors, producers and other executives born or educated in Florida and invited 500 to a party to be held February 9 at a Nikko hotel in Beverly Hills, Reitzammer said in an interview.
The council is soon to open a New York office to solicit filmed-entertainment production, Reitzammer said.
